COMPLETED_REQUIREMENTS.title: Completed requirements
COMPLETED_REQUIREMENTS.content: An unfinished structure is not generally a completed technology unlock. Building existence, completion, local attachment, power, placement, producer availability, and resource affordability are separate conditions. A construction start proves an order reached the game; it does not prove the structure will complete. Losing a prerequisite can remove access to future orders even while already existing units remain usable.

TERRAN_CONSTRUCTION_AND_REPAIR.title: Terran construction and repair
TERRAN_CONSTRUCTION_AND_REPAIR.content: An SCV must remain assigned to construct an ordinary Terran building; if it leaves or dies, another SCV can resume unfinished construction. The incomplete building is not automatically lost with its original worker. Repair restores mechanical units and structures at a resource cost and occupies the repairing SCV or MULE. Mechanical is the relevant repair category, not simply belonging to Terran. Severely damaged Terran structures can burn down if left unattended.

LIFT_LAND_AND_ADD_ONS.title: Lift, land, and add-ons
LIFT_LAND_AND_ADD_ONS.content: Command Centers, Orbital Commands, Barracks, Factories, and Starports can lift; a Planetary Fortress cannot. A flying production building cannot train its normal products and cannot use an attached add-on. Landing needs a valid footprint. A Tech Lab unlocks advanced products for the building actually attached to it; a Reactor provides parallel production for compatible basic products. A detached add-on can be reused, but occupying the landing/add-on area can prevent reconnection. Add-on research and production are distinct activities.

PROTOSS_WARP_CONSTRUCTION_AND_POWER.title: Protoss warp construction and power
PROTOSS_WARP_CONSTRUCTION_AND_POWER.content: A Probe starts a building and is then free to move; the building continues warping in. Most Protoss structures need a power field, while Nexus, Pylon, and Assimilator are exceptions. Power is spatial: possessing a Pylon somewhere on the map is insufficient. Destroying a supporting Pylon or moving a phased Warp Prism can disable nearby structures. A disabled structure still occupies space and can be attacked.

WARP_GATE_PRODUCTION.title: Warp Gate production
WARP_GATE_PRODUCTION.content: Warp Gate research unlocks conversion of individual Gateways. A Warp Gate places an eligible ground unit in a legal power field and then has a cooldown; it does not use the ordinary Gateway queue in the same way. The unit is vulnerable while materializing. Warp-in duration depends on the supporting power source and its context, so distant Pylon power should not be assumed equivalent to a reinforced power field or Warp Prism. Non-Gateway units cannot be warped in by a Warp Gate.

ZERG_CONSTRUCTION_AND_CREEP.title: Zerg construction and creep
ZERG_CONSTRUCTION_AND_CREEP.content: A Drone becomes a building, reducing the worker population. Most Zerg buildings require creep for placement; Hatchery and Extractor are important exceptions. Creep spreads from sources and recedes after those sources are removed. It supports Zerg movement and construction but is not a Protoss-style power supply: losing nearby creep is not equivalent to powering off all Zerg production. Creep can prevent Terran and Protoss construction on otherwise open ground.

LARVA_AND_INJECTS.title: Larva and injects
LARVA_AND_INJECTS.content: Hatcheries, Lairs, and Hives generate Larva. Drones, most army units, and Overlords share this production resource. A Queen's Spawn Larva adds Larva to a town hall after a delay; an accepted inject is not immediate army production. Queens themselves are trained at the town hall rather than from Larva. Town-hall morphs retain the same base site; adding a tech building does not create a second independent Larva source.

MORPHS_FORMS_AND_ALIASES.title: Morphs, forms, and aliases
MORPHS_FORMS_AND_ALIASES.content: A morph consumes or transforms its source: Lair from Hatchery, Hive from Lair, Lurker from Hydralisk, and Brood Lord from Corruptor. A form change such as Tank siege mode or lowered Depot is a different state of the same asset. Tech aliases allow higher or alternate forms to satisfy specified prerequisites. A form's separate API type ID does not establish a new purchasable unit or a new production queue.
